question: A 24-year-old woman presents with thin, grey-white vaginal discharge with an offensive fishy odour. Wet mount shows absence of lactobacilli and clue cells comprising >20% of epithelial cells. The whiff test is positive. Vaginal pH is 5.2. According to Amsel criteria, how many criteria does she meet, and does this confirm a diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis?

answers.text: Two criteria — not sufficient to diagnose BV (three of four required)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Count again: (1) thin, grey-white discharge; (2) pH >4.5 (pH 5.2); (3) positive whiff test; (4) clue cells >20% on wet mount. She meets all four criteria. Three of four are required, so four of four definitely confirms BV.

answers.text: Three criteria — sufficient to confirm bacterial vaginosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: She actually meets all four Amsel criteria: characteristic discharge, elevated pH (5.2 > 4.5), positive whiff test, and clue cells >20%. All four are present, not three. Three of four are sufficient, so four of four also confirms BV.

answers.text: Four criteria — confirms bacterial vaginosis (three of four required for diagnosis)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. All four Amsel criteria are met: (1) homogeneous grey-white discharge; (2) vaginal pH >4.5; (3) positive amine (whiff) test; (4) clue cells >20% of epithelial cells. Meeting three of the four criteria is sufficient for BV diagnosis; four of four makes it definitive.

answers.text: Four criteria — but confirms Trichomonas vaginalis, not BV

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Amsel criteria are specific for bacterial vaginosis, not Trichomonas. Trichomonas presents with frothy, yellow-green discharge and motile trichomonads on wet mount. Clue cells and positive whiff test are hallmarks of BV.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Amsel criteria for BV: (1) homogeneous grey-white discharge, (2) vaginal pH >4.5, (3) positive amine (whiff) test with 10% KOH, (4) clue cells >20% on wet mount. Three of four = BV. This patient meets all four.

Correct. Four Amsel criteria present, confirming BV. Remember: BV = clue cells + fishy whiff + pH >4.5 + grey-white discharge. Three of four required. Treatment: metronidazole 400–500 mg orally twice daily for 7 days.
